timeline.title: Severe Thanksgiving Storm Causes Widespread Flooding and Power Outages
timeline.summary: A powerful storm impacted the East Coast during Thanksgiving, resulting in significant flooding and widespread power outages. Nearly 1 million customers experienced power loss, with reports indicating that around 940,000 were affected at the peak of the outages. Cleanup efforts are underway as millions deal with the aftermath of the storm, which brought heavy rain and high winds, toppling trees and flooding streets.

event_overview.title: About Day Storm
event_overview.subject: Day Storm
event_overview.summary: “Day Storm” refers here to the Midwest-to-Eastern U.S. Thanksgiving storm of November 2026, a strong low-pressure system that developed near the Southeast coast and moved north along the East Coast during the Thanksgiving holiday. It combined heavy rain, damaging winds and coastal flooding in the East with wintry precipitation in parts of the Mid-Mississippi Valley, disrupting travel and public events.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The system developed on November 25, 2026, intensified and moved up the East Coast through Thanksgiving on November 26, and continued to produce impacts into November 27.

facts.label: Storm type and track
facts.value: The National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center characterized it as a strong coastal storm: low pressure formed off the Southeast coast and tracked northeastward along the Eastern Seaboard.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: Its principal coastal hazards extended from the Carolinas into the Northeast, while associated winter weather affected parts of the Mid-Mississippi Valley, including Missouri.

facts.label: Main hazards
facts.value: Forecast and warning materials identified heavy rain, strong winds, major coastal flooding, beach erosion and some wintry precipitation as the central hazards; coastal flood warnings extended from North Carolina to southern Connecticut at the storm's peak.

facts.label: Notable public-event disruption
facts.value: In New York City, officials postponed the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade from Thanksgiving Day to Saturday, November 28, citing expected high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major Thanksgiving-week disruptions, including the parade postponement and flooding and power-outage impacts; it does not aim to document every local forecast, warning, damage report, restoration update or travel disruption caused by the broader storm.
